quotes.text: Define the state you want, watch for drift from that state, decide what the drift means, then take action automatically.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises the whole self-healing pattern in one sentence.

quotes.text: Rules without runtime enforcement become backlog. Reviews without correction become theater, and human oversight, no matter how smart the people are, loses the race once creation speed exceeds review speed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp explanation of why manual governance fails at scale.

quotes.text: If your architecture can't contain oversharing fast, AI adoption stalls. Not because the assistant failed, but because the tenant underneath it never learned how to recover fast enough.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links Copilot adoption directly to remediation speed.

quotes.text: If you build your architecture on the assumption that the platform will always accept your pace, the whole design starts lying to you under stress.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns that automation must be designed around platform limits.

chapters.title: From controls to a self-healing system
Failure mode 2: Teams and private channel sprawl

takeaways: Governance written as documentation cannot keep up with a changing tenant; the metric that matters is how long drift stays alive before it is fixed.
A self-healing architecture separates signals, desired state, orchestration, enforcement and audit, and is tested by failures like Copilot oversharing and Teams sprawl.
Build the remediation engine on Microsoft Graph, Logic Apps and managed identity, with queues, back-off with jitter and pagination so throttling does not break it.
hook: Your Microsoft 365 tenant changes faster than any review board can check it. This episode is for architects and admins who want to move from manual governance to a self-healing remediation engine that detects and fixes drift automatically, without collapsing under Graph throttling.
